name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
short_description: One of the most famous Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on the western bank of the holy river Ganga in Varanasi.
historical_background: The temple has been referred to in Hindu scriptures for millennia as a central part of Shaivism. The current temple structure was constructed by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore in 1780 after historical demolitions.
religious_cultural_significance: It stands as one of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas. Devotees believe a pilgrimage to Kashi Vishwanath and taking a dip in the holy River Ganga leads to Moksha (liberation).
dress_code: Traditional Indian attire is encouraged. Dhoti/Kurta for men and Saree/Salwar Kameez for women. Leather items, mobile phones, and electronic items are strictly prohibited inside the main sanctum.
visitor_guidelines: Carry valid government ID. Utilize official locker facilities outside the temple corridor. Follow queue discipline during heavy festive rush.
best_time_to_visit: October to March during the pleasant winter climate of Northern India.
location_information: Situated in Lahori Tola, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh near Dashashwamedh Ghat along the Ganges riverfront corridor.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India & Ministry of Tourism

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
short_description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site built by Chola Emperor Rajaraja I in 1010 AD, renowned for its massive Dravidian architecture and monumental vimana.
historical_background: Built entirely of granite between 1003 and 1010 AD by King Rajaraja I, this temple showcases the pinnacle of Chola empire stone architecture and bronze metallurgy.
religious_cultural_significance: Represents a landmark masterpiece of South Indian temple architecture, housing one of the largest monolithic Shiva Lingams and single-stone Nandi statues in India.
dress_code: Respectful, modest clothing. Shoulders and knees must be covered. Footwear must be deposited at the entrance gateway (Gopuram).
visitor_guidelines: Photography is permitted in outer courtyards but strictly prohibited inside the main sanctum. Please do not touch or lean on ancient stone carvings.
best_time_to_visit: November to February during pleasant weather in Tamil Nadu.
location_information: Located on Membalam Road, Balaganapathy Nagar, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu 613007.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
short_description: An ancient historic temple situated on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, famed for its 14 colorful sculptured gopurams.
historical_background: Mentioned in early Tamil Sangam literature. Major expansions were executed under the Pandyan rulers and later magnificently restored by Nayak dynasty rulers in the 16th-17th centuries.
religious_cultural_significance: A premier pilgrimage center in Shaktism and Shaivism housing the iconic Hall of 1000 Pillars and sacred Golden Lotus Tank (Porthamarai Kulam).
dress_code: Traditional dress required. Dhoti/Pants for men and Saree/Salwar for women. Western shorts and sleeveless tops are strictly prohibited.
visitor_guidelines: Electronic items and mobile phones are prohibited inside temple premises. Deposit them in official lockers at entrance gopurams.
location_information: Located at Madurai Main, Madurai, Tamil Nadu 625001.

name: Somnath Temple
short_description: Revered as the first of the twelve holy Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva, situated on the coast of the Arabian Sea in Prabhas Patan.
historical_background: Mentioned in Rigveda and Skanda Purana. Rebuilt several times throughout history; the present majestic temple was constructed in Maru-Gurjara style in 1951.
religious_cultural_significance: Symbolizes eternal resilience and spiritual sanctity. The Banastambha (arrow pillar) on the sea wall points directly to Antarctica without any landmass in between.
dress_code: Decent, modest clothing. Shorts and revealing outfits are not allowed.
visitor_guidelines: Strict security screening at entrance. Mobiles, cameras, and electronic gadgets must be stored in free lockers before entering.
best_time_to_visit: November to February during pleasant coastal weather.
location_information: Prabhas Patan, Veraval, Gujarat 362268 on the Arabian coastline.

name: Konark Sun Temple
short_description: A 13th-century Sun Temple built by King Narasimhadeva I, designed as a giant stone chariot with 24 intricate wheels drawn by 7 horses.
historical_background: Constructed around 1250 AD in Kalinga architectural style. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.
religious_cultural_significance: A monumental landmark of Indian temple architecture celebrating solar worship and astronomical science through carved stone sundial wheels.
dress_code: Casual modest clothing suitable for outdoor heritage site walking.
visitor_guidelines: Entry ticket required via ASI portal or scanner. Avoid touching or climbing on protected stone sculptures and chariot wheels.
location_information: Konark, Puri district, Odisha 752111, off the Bay of Bengal coast.

name: Jagannath Temple
short_description: A sacred Char Dham pilgrimage site famous for its sacred wooden deities and world-renowned annual Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival).
historical_background: Constructed in the 12th century AD by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.
religious_cultural_significance: Represents the heart of Odia cultural identity and Vaishnava devotion. Celebrated for Mahaprasad prepared in traditional clay pots in the world's largest temple kitchen.
dress_code: Strict traditional attire. Leather items, electronic devices, and cameras are prohibited inside temple premises.
visitor_guidelines: Non-Hindus can view temple compound from Raghunandan Library roof. Follow queue guidance provided by temple administration.
best_time_to_visit: November to February (and June/July for Rath Yatra).
source_name: Shree Jagannath Temple Administration (SJTA) & Odisha Tourism

name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
short_description: Situated on Seshachalam Hills in Tirumala, this is one of the most visited and sacred hill pilgrimage shrines in the world.
historical_background: Patronized by major South Indian dynasties including Pallavas, Cholas, Hoysalas, and Vijayanagara emperors such as Sri Krishnadevaraya.
religious_cultural_significance: Believed to be Kali Yuga Vaikuntam. Famous for GI-tagged Tirupati Laddu Prasadam and sacred tonsuring rituals.
darshan_timings: 03:00 AM - 01:30 AM (Open 22 Hours daily via queue complexes)
dress_code: Strictly enforced. Men must wear Dhoti/Kurta. Women must wear Saree, Half-Saree, or Chudidhar with Dupatta. Jeans and T-shirts are prohibited in darshan lines.
visitor_guidelines: Book advance slot tokens online via TTD official portal. Wear RFID wristbands for young children. Security checkpoint mandatory at Alipiri.
location_information: Tirumala Hills, Tirupati, Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh 517504.

name: Kedarnath Temple
short_description: A revered mountain temple nestled in the Garhwal Himalayan range near Mandakini river at an altitude of 3,583 meters above sea level.
historical_background: Believed to have been originally established by Pandavas and later revived by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century AD.
religious_cultural_significance: One of the highest sacred Jyotirlingas and a key shrine of the Chota Char Dham pilgrimage of Uttarakhand.
dress_code: Warm heavy woollens, comfortable trekking boots, and modest clothing suited for Himalayan high-altitude weather.
visitor_guidelines: Mandatory Chardham Yatra registration required. Physical fitness verification recommended. Trek distance is 16 km from Gaurikund (Helicopter & Pony services available).
best_time_to_visit: May to June and September to October (Closed Nov to April due to snow).
